q: The Italian scientist Evangelista Torricelli first noticed the variation of pressure due to height and time.
e: Evangelista Torricelli was the first to observe and document pressure variations with height and time.

q: Evangelista Torricelli invented and constructed a barometer in 1644.
e: The barometer was invented and constructed by Torricelli in the year 1644.

q: Evangelista Torricelli invented and constructed a barometer in 1466.
e: Evangelista Torricelli invented and constructed a barometer in 1644, not 1466.

q: The barometer is a device for measuring atmospheric pressure.
e: A barometer is specifically designed to measure atmospheric pressure.

q: The barometer is a device for measuring liquid pressure.
e: The barometer is a device for measuring atmospheric pressure, not liquid pressure.

q: A simple mercury barometer consists of a glass tube about 1 metre long sealed at one end and filled with mercury.
e: This is the exact construction of a simple mercury barometer.

q: A simple mercury barometer consists of a glass tube about 1 metre long open at both ends and filled with water.
e: It consists of a glass tube sealed at one end and filled with mercury, not open at both ends with water.

q: The tube is then inverted and the open end is submerged in a reservoir of mercury.
e: This is the correct procedure for setting up a simple mercury barometer.

q: The mercury column is held up by the pressure of the atmosphere acting on the surface of mercury in the reservoir.
e: Atmospheric pressure on the reservoir surface supports the mercury column in the tube.

q: The mercury column is held up by the vacuum at the top of the tube.
e: The mercury column is held up by the pressure of the atmosphere acting on the surface of mercury in the reservoir.

q: The atmospheric pressure in terms of height of mercury column in a barometer is $p = \rho g h$.
e: This is the standard formula for calculating pressure from a fluid column height.

q: The atmospheric pressure in terms of height of mercury column in a barometer is $p = \rho g / h$.
e: The correct formula is $p = \rho g h$, not $p = \rho g / h$.

q: $760 \text{ mm Hg}$ is the atmospheric pressure at sea level and is known as standard atmospheric pressure.
e: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is defined as $760 \text{ mm Hg}$.

q: $760 \text{ mm Hg}$ is the atmospheric pressure at the top of a mountain and is known as standard atmospheric pressure.
e: $760 \text{ mm Hg}$ is the atmospheric pressure at sea level, not at the top of a mountain.

q: Standard atmospheric pressure is also known as 1 atmosphere (1 atm).
e: 1 atm is the standard abbreviation for standard atmospheric pressure.

q: The density of mercury $\rho$ is $13590 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
e: The standard density of mercury used in these calculations is $13590 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

q: The density of mercury $\rho$ is $1360 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
e: The density of mercury is $13590 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, not $1360 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

q: The acceleration due to gravity $g$ is taken as $9.8 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ for standard atmospheric pressure calculation.
e: The standard value of $g$ used is $9.8 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

q: The height of the mercury column $h$ at standard atmospheric pressure is $760 \text{ mm}$ (or $0.760 \text{ m}$).
e: Standard atmospheric pressure corresponds to a mercury column height of $760 \text{ mm}$.

q: The standard atmospheric pressure is $1.013 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.
e: Calculated as $13590 \times 9.8 \times 0.760$, the standard atmospheric pressure is $1.013 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.

q: The standard atmospheric pressure is $1.013 \times 10^3 \text{ Pa}$.
e: The standard atmospheric pressure is $1.013 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$, not $10^3 \text{ Pa}$.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 1013 \text{ hPa}$.
e: 1 atmosphere is equivalent to 1013 hectopascals.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 1.01 \text{ bar}$.
e: 1 atmosphere is approximately equal to 1.01 bar.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 14.7 \text{ lb in}^{-2}$ (psi).
e: 1 atmosphere is equivalent to 14.7 pounds per square inch.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 760 \text{ torr}$.
e: 1 atmosphere is exactly equal to 760 torr.

q: The vertical height of the mercury column depends on the tilt of the column.
e: The vertical height of the mercury column does not depend on the tilt of the column.

q: The vertical height of the mercury column is independent of the diameter (width) of the tube.
e: The vertical height remains unaffected by the tube's diameter or width.

q: The vertical height of the mercury column depends only on the pressure outside the tube.
e: The external atmospheric pressure is the sole determinant of the vertical mercury column height.

q: If the tube is lowered below $760 \text{ mm}$, the mercury would completely fill the tube.
e: Lowering the tube below the standard height causes the mercury to completely fill it.

q: The action of sucking a liquid by a drinking straw increases the volume of the lungs, thereby reducing the air pressure in the lungs and the mouth.
e: Reduced pressure in the mouth allows higher atmospheric pressure to push the liquid up the straw.

q: When the piston of a syringe is pulled up, the pressure inside the cylinder decreases.
e: Pulling the piston increases volume, which decreases the internal pressure, allowing atmospheric pressure to drive liquid in.

q: When pressing on a smooth surface, most of the air inside the rubber sucker is squeezed out and the pressure is reduced.
e: The reduced internal pressure allows external atmospheric pressure to hold the sucker in position.
